# Version constraints for the Python packages installed on a device by setup.sh.
#
# GENERATED — do not edit by hand. Regenerate with:
#   uv export --frozen --no-dev --no-hashes --no-emit-project > config/device-constraints.txt
# tests/test_device_constraints.py fails if this drifts from uv.lock.
#
# Used as a pip CONSTRAINTS file (-c), not a requirements file: it pins versions for
# whatever gets installed without itself installing anything. That matters because the
# fleet takes six of its Python packages from apt (see config/apt/manual-packages.txt)
# and only the rest from pip, and a requirements file would install pip copies of all of
# them.
#
# Why this exists: setup.sh used to pip install a hand-written list with --upgrade, whose
# default --upgrade-strategy=only-if-needed upgrades named packages but leaves transitive
# ones alone. icalendar is transitive via recurring-ical-events, so it sat at 7.0.3 on
# every kiosk while uv.lock said 7.2.2 — and any future transitive dep would freeze the
# same way. Constraining the whole resolved closure fixes the class, not the instance.
#
# KNOWN RESIDUAL: this pins only what pip installs. The packages that come from apt keep
# Debian's versions, so they can still sit behind the lockfile — as of 2026-08-21 the Pi
# fleet runs packaging 25.0 (lock: 26.3), psutil 7.0.0 (lock: 7.2.2), and greenlet 3.1.0
# (lock: 3.3.1). Closing that gap means either letting pip own those too or relaxing their
# pyproject pins to match Debian; both are bigger decisions than this file.
#
# This file was autogenerated by uv via the following command:
#    uv export --frozen --no-dev --no-hashes --no-emit-project
